title: mshta.exe inline vbscript: proxy execution with a reconnaissance payload

alert.rule_name: Defense Evasion: mshta.exe Executed Inline Script Without an HTA File

mitre_attack.technique: T1218.005 - System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta

alert.description: mshta.exe was invoked with a vbscript: or javascript: URI on its command line rather than a path to an .hta file. In that form mshta acts as a general-purpose script interpreter, which is used to run code under the identity of a signed Microsoft binary and to bypass application-control policies that permit mshta.exe.
alert.detection_logic: Sysmon EventID=1 (ProcessCreate) WHERE Image ENDSWITH '\mshta.exe' AND CommandLine MATCHES ANY ('vbscript:', 'javascript:', 'about:') AND CommandLine NOT MATCHES '\.hta'

enrichment.technique_note: mshta.exe launched with a 'vbscript:Execute(...)' URI executes the supplied script directly. There is no .hta file on disk and no remote URL in this invocation, so there is no downloaded artifact to analyse — everything the process did is on its command line.
enrichment.command_chain: mshta.exe creates a Wscript.Shell COM object and calls .Run on it, which spawns powershell.exe. The observed lineage is cmd.exe -> mshta.exe -> powershell.exe -> conhost.exe.
enrichment.payload_content: The command the payload actually runs is 'powershell -noexit -command Get-Service sysmon'. Get-Service queries the state of a named Windows service; 'sysmon' is the endpoint telemetry agent. The command reads service state and does not stop, disable, reconfigure or delete anything. -noexit leaves the console open, which is characteristic of a human running a command interactively rather than an automated implant.
enrichment.what_is_absent: Within the captured window there are no outbound network connections, no DNS queries, no files written outside normal process working paths, no registry persistence writes, no service or scheduled-task creation, and no access to credential stores. The process tree terminates at the PowerShell console.
enrichment.account_and_parent: The user is WORKSTATION5\wardog, a local account, and the parent is an interactive cmd.exe session — consistent with someone typing at the console rather than remote or automated execution.

verdict.rationale: The chain uses an inline vbscript URI in mshta.exe to launch PowerShell and query the Sysmon service, which is a suspicious proxy-execution and security-software discovery pattern. The provided window also shows a high-integrity terminal session and limited follow-on behavior, including only normal-looking Recent-items file artifacts and no mshta/PowerShell network events observed in the provided chain. Without customer authorization or change context, intent remains unresolved and escalation is safer than either automated closure or immediate containment.

acceptable_alternatives.rationale: Malicious is defensible because O1 (R000284) records inline vbscript proxy execution through mshta and O3 (R000422, R000445) records the resulting PowerShell query of the Sysmon service. O4 (R000612, R000616) shows only routine shell artifacts, and the delivered window does not establish follow-on impact, so escalation remains required while authorization and intent are verified.
acceptable_alternatives.credit_rationale: This reading survives peer review because the invocation matches offensive proxy-execution and security-software-discovery tradecraft, but it receives half relief because the observed command is read-only and the delivered window shows no attributable network or follow-on impact.

observations.desc: PowerShell PID 9572 created temporary CustomDestinations files under the user's Recent directory in the provided window.

inferences.desc: Using mshta.exe with an inline vbscript URI to create PowerShell is consistent with signed-binary proxy execution rather than ordinary HTA-file use.
Querying the Sysmon service can provide awareness of endpoint monitoring, but the command alone does not establish hostile intent or an attempt to disable the service.

The high-integrity terminal session, narrow observed command, scoped lack of chain-attributable network events, and Recent-items file artifacts limit the demonstrated impact in the provided window but do not establish that the activity was authorized.

investigations.desc: Ask the customer whether WKS-4471\t.okafor was authorized to test this mshta technique or query the Sysmon service at the observed time.
Review the preceding cmd.exe activity and available session telemetry to identify how the inline mshta command was introduced.
Extend endpoint and network review beyond the provided window for the mshta and PowerShell process chain, including DNS and connection telemetry.
Verify the Sysmon service state and review subsequent service-control, registry, task, and process events for attempts to alter monitoring or establish persistence.
Inspect the PowerShell-created CustomDestinations artifacts and related user activity to confirm whether they are routine shell-history side effects.

unknowns.desc: Customer authorization, change-management, maintenance, and red-team context is unavailable.
The origin of the inline command and the operator's intent are not established by the provided telemetry.
Activity before or after the provided window, including any later network, persistence, or service-modification behavior, is unknown.
